items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: I had done a thing for Benny Goodman... Jerry was to deliver my scores... he brought the thing in to Benny and told me they went through it and Benny looked puzzled but gave him the check.

ctx.x: (Tape went blank for a few seconds)
--there was some fast work with clarinet and piano between Benny and
Mel and Mel indicated in his letter that when he came to those passages Benny would just look at his part instead of playing it, while Mel was playing his part.

items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: Benny and Teddy Wilson were very big

ctx.x: I was twenty in 1940. Right, it was about '38 at this time.
While I was downstairs, the Benny Goodman Trio, Gene Krupa and Benny and Teddy Wilson were very big, and Krupa came down to N.Y.U. to give a jazz concert.

He came down alone so they searched through the school to find a clarinet player and a piano player and they found me and another guy and we played the thing with Gene. I remember calling him a few years after that, when he formed
